vehicles.speed_basis: Normal (non-boost) top speed, 40 km/h, from the Battlefield 4 infobox on the Battlefield Wiki M1 Abrams page ('40 KPH Standard; 56 KPH Max'). The 56 km/h figure is the boost.
vehicles.note: This is the anchor tank, so method B is 1.0 by construction. Method B gives medium because validate.mjs maps 1 <= r <= 1.5 to medium. With boost, 56 km/h (15.56 m/s), method A is 2.393 and still fast. The page's trivia line '51 MPH' does not match the infobox, so I ignored it. Gamepressure's BF4 tank guide gives 56 km/h as 'top speed', which is the boost figure.

vehicles.speed_basis: Normal top speed, 42 km/h, from the Battlefield 4 infobox on the Battlefield Wiki LAV-25 page ('42 km/h, 65 km/h (boost), 28 km/h (in water)'). The BTR-90 has the same figures and the ZBD-09 has 42/64.
vehicles.note: With boost (65 km/h, 18.06 m/s), method A is 2.778, which is very-fast: the band flips. Boost against boost for method B is 65/56 = 1.161, still medium. Mixing bases, boosted LAV against the standard Abrams, gives 1.625, which is fast. Since BF3 the boost has no meter (Battlefield Wiki, Vehicle Boost), so it can be held indefinitely.

vehicles.speed_basis: No figure found. The Battlefield Wiki's BF4 infobox for the M1161 ITV (and for its counterparts, the VDV Buggy and the LYT2021/FAV) has no speed, only 'Fast attack vehicle' and maneuverability 'Fast'. The Symthic BF4 vehicle-stats thread could not be reached (the site is down and the archive is blocked).
vehicles.note: Judged. Light vehicles are the fastest BF4 ground vehicles after the quad bike (Prima eGuide summary) and outrun wheeled IFVs (42 km/h, 65 km/h boost). Anything above 58.5 km/h is already over 2.5x the 6.5 m/s sprint, so A = very-fast is fairly safe. For B I estimated about 65-95 km/h. BF4 compresses real speeds: the Abrams is 67 km/h in reality and 40 in game. The real Growler does 105 km/h cross-country. That estimate gives 1.6-2.4x the 40 km/h Abrams, which is fast. If the in-game top speed is over 100 km/h, B becomes very-fast.

vehicles.speed_basis: BF4 attack helicopter top speed '160 (RU, US)' from gamepressure's BF4 assault-helicopter guide. The guide calls it the game's own speed unit; I treated it as km/h. The Battlefield Wiki BF4 infobox gives no speed. Its BF3 infobox gives 330 km/h, and ludo.guide's 410 km/h looks like the real-world figure, so I rejected it.
vehicles.note: The raw number is uncertain (the unit is unclear, and the BF3 figure is 330 km/h), but every candidate figure gives very-fast under both methods: the 330 km/h figure gives A 14.1 and B 8.25. A forum snippet relaying Symthic in-game timings (scout heli about 125 km/h against a listed 120) suggests the HUD units are roughly km/h. Under method B every aircraft lands in very-fast against a tank, so B gives no spread for air units.

vehicles.speed_basis: Stock top speed on level ground, 66 km/h, from the in-game speedometer as reported by the Steam 'Tank guide' (posted Feb 2018, updated Oct 2020). The PlanetSide 2 Wiki gives no vehicle speeds; Prowler/Main only says it 'boasts a higher top speed' than the other MBTs.
vehicles.note: This is the anchor tank, so method B is 1.0 by construction, which is medium. A 2013 Daybreak forum post gives about 60 km/h stock (70 with Racer 3). That gives A = 2.564, still very-fast but close to the 2.5 line. Under method A, very-fast is outside the bands the tracks mobility allows (very-slow to fast), so the validator would flag the unit as ATYPICAL.

vehicles.speed_basis: Stock top speed on level ground, 'about 70kph', from the same Steam 'Tank guide' (2018/2020). The PlanetSide 2 Wiki Lightning/Main says only that it is 'faster, more maneuverable and smaller' than the MBTs.
vehicles.note: Against a 60 km/h Prowler, B = 1.167, still medium. As with the Prowler, A = very-fast breaks the tracks mobility's allowed speed bands.

vehicles.speed_basis: Stock top speed of 90 km/h ('Has a top speed of 90KPH! (Unupgraded vehicle)'), not counting turbo, from the Steam guide 'The Harasser' (posted May 2013, updated May 2025). With max Racer it reaches 110 km/h. The wiki says only that it has 'high speed' and a turbo.
vehicles.note: The 90 km/h figure may date from 2013. Against a 60 km/h Prowler, B = 1.5 exactly: medium under the validator's r <= 1.5 rule, but on the line. A Harasser with full Racer (110 km/h) gives B = 1.667, which is fast.

vehicles.speed_basis: No figure found. The PlanetSide 2 Wiki has none. The Steam 'Complete Sunderer Guide' (2014) says that on even ground it is 'only beaten in speed by the Lightning tank and the Harrasser buggy'. The July 9, 2024 update rolled the full level-3 Racer and Rival chassis stats into its base stats.
vehicles.note: Judged. The 2014 guide places it between the Prowler (66 km/h) and the Lightning (70 km/h) on flat ground, and the 2024 change only made it faster, so I put it at about 66-75 km/h. That is over 2.5x the 6.5 m/s sprint (A very-fast) and about 1.0-1.15x the Prowler (B medium). If it were slightly slower than the Prowler, B would drop to slow.

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed, 5.42 m/s (offspeed field), from the Foxhole Wiki (foxhole.wiki.gg) infobox and its Movement Speed table. The road speed is 7.75.
vehicles.note: This is the anchor tank, so method B is 1.0, which is medium. Against the sprint speed (about 7.2 m/s), A would be 0.753, which is slow. On roads A would be 1.55, fast. Petrol adds 10% to top speed, and tier 2/3 roads add 2.5% or 5%.

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed, 5.79 m/s, from the Foxhole Wiki infobox (offspeed) and its Movement Speed table. The road speed is 8.27.
vehicles.note: On roads it is still medium under B (8.27/7.75 = 1.067) and fast under A (1.654).

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed, 3.27 m/s, from the Foxhole Wiki infobox (offspeed) and its Movement Speed table. The road speed is 10.88.
vehicles.note: The wiki calls its mobility 'mediocre off-road speed and decent on-road speed'. On roads it would be fast under A (2.176) and medium under B (1.404). This is a wheeled armoured car, and the wheels mobility allows only medium, fast and very-fast, so the off-road basis makes it ATYPICAL under both methods ('mobility:wheels allowed.speed-bands very-slow').

vehicles.speed_basis: Off-road top speed at 0% encumbrance, 3.46 m/s, from the Foxhole Wiki infobox (offspeed) and its Movement Speed table. Off-road is 2.77 at 1-99% load and 2.49 at 100%+; road is 17.32 / 13.86 / 12.47.
vehicles.note: A = 0.692 sits just under the 0.7 line. Trucks are road vehicles: on roads A would be 3.464 (very-fast) and B 2.235 (fast), the biggest road/off-road swing of all twelve vehicles. As with the O'Brien, very-slow breaks the wheels mobility's allowed bands. Confidence is medium because of the basis choice, not the figure.

unclear:
1) Band edges. speed-bands.json overlaps at 1.0 ('0.7 to 1' for slow, '1 to 1.5' for medium) and does not say which band 1.5 or 2.5 belongs to. I used the rule in scripts/validate.mjs: r<0.7 very-slow, r<1 slow, r<=1.5 medium, r<=2.5 fast, else very-fast. Under method B the anchor tank is always exactly 1.0, so every anchor is medium only because of this rule. Two values sit on edges: the PS2 Harasser against a 60 km/h Prowler is exactly 1.5, and the Foxhole Dunne Transport under A is 0.692.

2) Boost in Battlefield. Since BF3 the vehicle boost has no meter (Battlefield Wiki, Vehicle Boost), so it can be held like the unlimited sprint used for the soldier reference. That argues for boosted speeds, but I followed the task and used standard speeds. With boost, the LAV-25 flips from fast to very-fast under A (2.78). Gamepressure lists the boost figures as 'top speed' (tank 56, IFV 65), so coders may differ. Method B also needs a rule that both speeds use the same basis: a boosted LAV against the standard Abrams is 1.625, which is fast.

3) Foxhole road versus off-road. Off-road speeds make both wheeled vehicles very-slow under both methods (O'Brien 0.65/0.60, Dunne 0.69/0.64). On roads they are fast or very-fast. The wheels mobility allows only medium, fast and very-fast, so both would be ATYPICAL ('mobility:wheels allowed.speed-bands very-slow') whichever method is used.

4) Method A and tracks. Under A, PS2 tracked tanks (Prowler 2.82, Lightning 2.99) are very-fast, which the tracks mobility does not allow ('mobility:tracks allowed.speed-bands very-fast'). Method B removes this.

5) Soldier reference basis. Foxhole uses walking speed (5 m/s), while Battlefield and PS2 use sprint (6.5 m/s). Using Foxhole's sprint (about 7.2 m/s) would move the Silverhand under A from medium to slow.

6) What method B separates. B fixes PS2, where A puts everything very-fast. But B puts all four PS2 ground vehicles in medium (1.0-1.36), so it still does not separate them. Every aircraft becomes very-fast against a tank (Viper 4.0x). B also puts infantry (method A) and vehicles (method B) on different scales in the same field, so typed links that compare speed across units (e.g. speed:>=fast) would mix scales.

7) Weak figures. PS2 speeds are community speedometer readings from 2013-2020 guides, not wiki data. BF4 has no ITV figure, and its helicopter figure is in unclear 'game units' (taken as km/h). The two judged bands (ITV B fast, Sunderer B medium) are the least certain; ITV B becomes very-fast if its true speed is over 100 km/h.
